taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Bank-road, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 640 | 5.21 | 5.21
2 | 934 | 8.58 | 13.8
3 | 2594 | 84.1 | 97.9
4 | 4386 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Bank-road, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Bank-road Station, Bori Metropolis**

The VES interpretation at Bank-road reveals a four-layer subsurface sequence with resistivity increasing monotonically with depth:

- Layer 1: 640 Ω·m (0–5.21 m)
- Layer 2: 934 Ω·m (5.21–13.8 m)
- Layer 3: 2594 Ω·m (13.8–97.9 m)
- Layer 4: 4386 Ω·m (below 97.9 m)

Checking successive triplets: Layers 1-2-3 (640 < 934 < 2594) give an A pattern, and Layers 2-3-4 (934 < 2594 < 4386) also give an A pattern. The curve is therefore correctly classified as AA-type, consistent with a steadily increasing resistivity profile, likely indicating progressively more resistive (possibly more consolidated or coarser) formations with depth. No contradictions were found between the resistivity values and the stated curve type. The on-file classification is confirmed accurate for drilling planning purposes.

{"curve_type_stated": "AA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
